newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks dip with Dow at open, banks hit.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks dip with Dow at open, banks hit.

text.p: The Australian share market dipped with the Dow at the opening on Monday with big banks again receiving a battering.
The All Ordinaries index lost eight points to 2,530.1.
Sellers again attacked the big banks, the sector index losing 1.3 percent early, with only interest in major miners, BHP, CRA and WMC limiting early overall losses.
"The miners are looking good but the rest is looking a bit ordinary," said head of equities at Intersuisse, Andrew Sekely, adding that the interest in the resource leaders could continue.
"It could continue quite strongly. The miners have been sluggish for a while and a big run might not be uncalled for."
Bellwether and copper major BHP added 19.1 cents to A$18.88 (US$14.54), CRA jumped 1.3 percent to A$20.67, while gold/nickel miner WMC added 1.2 percent to A$18.18.
The big banks were the lead in the saddlebags. The big four lost over one percent with Commonwealth Bank worst hit.
CommBank lost 37 cents or about 2.6 percent to A$13.75 while sector leader National Australia Bank lost 19 cents to A$17.76.
ANZ Bank lost 13 cents to A$8.20 while Westpac Banking Corporation dipped nine to A$7.15.
Falls outnumbered rises by a ratio of about nine to four, while about 38 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
